extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, playwrights, students of comedy, and general readers interested in the theory and practice of comic writing
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and prescriptive principles for composing and judging comedy (especially comic drama / comedy of manners), drawn from George Meredith's essay on the comic spirit. Focuses on audience, artistic gifts, style of wit, realism vs generalization, and moral/ideational aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivated audience required
rubrics_metrics.description: A society of cultivated men and women is required, wherein ideas are current and the perceptions quick, that he may be supplied with matter and an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that semi-barbarism, feverish emotional periods, and marked social inequality repel the Comic poet. Comedy needs an audience with intellectual activity to supply matter and to appreciate subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety and delicacy in the comic poet
rubrics_metrics.description: To touch and kindle the mind through laughter, demands more than sprightliness, a most subtle delicacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subtlety is a natal gift; without it the comic poet's work will be crude and will 'show him a startling exhibition of the dyer's hand'. The poet must aim at the head (the intellect), not merely provoke physical laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim at the mind (head), not merely the body
rubrics_metrics.description: People are ready to surrender themselves to witty thumps on the back, breast, and sides; all except the head: and it is there that he aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good comedy targets understanding and insight rather than mere noisy amusement or physical mirth; the comic effect should enlighten or provoke thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pandering to non-laughers and excessive-laughers
rubrics_metrics.description: There are men... agelasts (non-laughers) and hypergelasts (the excessive laughers)… to laugh at everything is to have no appreciation of the Comic of Comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy should not be tailored either to those who never laugh nor to those who laugh at everything; overly broad or indiscriminate joking ('to laugh at everything') flattens comic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position comedy between Puritan and Bacchanalian extremes
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall find ourselves about where the Comic spirit would place us, if we stand at middle distance between the inveterate opponents and the drum-and-fife supporters of Comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy must avoid being judged as libertine by moralists (Puritans) or as mere riotous license by its defenders (Bacchanalians); the proper stance is balanced seriousness and humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe manners and generalize (Moliere's Horatian precept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moliere followed the Horatian precept, to observe the manners of his age and give his characters the colour befitting them at the time. He did not paint in raw realism... and by slightly raising and softening the object of study ... generalized upon it so as to make it permanently human.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good comic characterization studies contemporary manners but raises/softens particulars into generalized, permanent types rather than mere raw portraiture; this secures lasting human relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid raw realism; realism without idea is merely 'remuage'
rubrics_metrics.description: In the realistic comedy it is an incessant remuage--no calm, merely bustling figures, and no thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realistic bustle and surface portraiture (mere imitating of life) without an underlying idea yields shallow comedy; critics should prefer works where realism serves an idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy must contain an underlying idea (the life of the comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The life of the comedy is in the idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plots or fables that are thin cannot supply the life; the comic work should be driven by an idea or central conception (as in Misanthrope), not by contrived incidents alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and reasoning should be organic, not preachy
rubrics_metrics.description: His moral does not hang like a tail, or preach from one character incessantly cocking an eye at the audience... but is in the heart of his work, throbbing with every pulsation of an organic structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy should vindicate reason and common-sense from within the structure of the play; moral lessons must arise naturally from character and situation rather than being tacked on or didactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cast characters as types serving the central purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: He seized his characters firmly for the central purpose of the play, stamped them in the idea...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should be drawn to embody and advance the central idea of the comedy; generalization (stamping in the idea) helps make them permanently human and illustrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit should spring from depth and reason, not surface cleverness
rubrics_metrics.description: Congreve's wit is a Toledo blade, sharp... To shine, it must have an adversary. Moliere's wit is like a running brook... it is full of healing, the wit of good breeding, the wit of wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface repartee and prepared quips (brilliant outsider wit) are shallow compared to wit that arises from understanding and moral insight; prefer wit that flows organically from characters and situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for an upper-class or lively social model for Comedy of Manners
rubrics_metrics.description: A simply bourgeois circle will not furnish it, for the middle class must have the brilliant, flippant, independent upper for a spur and a pattern; otherwise it is likely to be inwardly dull as well as outwardly correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy of manners thrives where there is contrast between classes and a lively upper-class world to observe and imitate; a purely bourgeois setting may lack the material for certain comic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy as corrective: expose and teach, not merely mock
rubrics_metrics.description: The Femmes Savantes is a capital instance of the uses of comedy in teaching the world to understand what ails it... The comedy... exposed the later ... absurdity... and the tendency to be idiotic in precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy can satirize and correct social follies by exposing them vividly; repetition and performance help the public see the cause of their error and reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scourge vice with self-mastery; purity in comic correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Never did man wield so shrieking a scourge upon vice, but his consummate self-mastery is not shaken while administering it... He conceives purely, and he writes purely...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when attacking vice, the comic artist should maintain moral purity and self-control in treatment—stripping folly rather than indulging in filthy or cynical license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of conception — avoid repetition of stock situations
rubrics_metrics.description: The later imitations... became tiresome, notwithstanding their fun, in the perpetual recurring of the same situations, owing to the absence of original study and vigour of conception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recycling stock plots and repeated situations produces boredom; comedy needs original study and vigorous conception to remain effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character vividness and voice over contrived plot
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a picturesqueness... You hear the tones, and see the sketch and colour of the whole scene in reading it... The life of the comedy is in the idea. The fable is thin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinctive character voices (e.g., Millamant) and vivid character-drawing give life to comedy even when plot is slight; prioritize character and idea over elaborate plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit and puns must have meaning and interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The source of his wit is clear reason: it is a fountain of that soil; and it springs to vindicate reason... The wit is of such pervading spirit that it inspires a pun with meaning and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wordplay and puns should be grounded in thought and significance; cleverness for its own sake (punch-lines without substance) is inferior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid idle empty laughter as the primary aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Believe that idle empty laughter is the most desirable of recreations, and significant Comedy will seem pale and shallow in comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the aim is simply to provoke superficial merriment, comedy loses depth and significance; significant comedy balances merriment with insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic poet is rare and requires a special gift
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a natal gift in the Comic poet... people are ready to surrender themselves to witty thumps... and it is there that he aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good comic creation is uncommon; it requires innate talent plus cultivation—do not assume comic skill is easily acquired by technique alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience acuteness is necessary to receive subtle comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: A corresponding acuteness must exist to welcome him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subtle comic work expects and relies on an intelligent audience capable of perceiving nuance; without such an audience the work may fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy elevates and showcases women's wit and common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy is the fountain of sound sense... Comedy lifts women to a station offering them free play for their wit... Dorine in the Tartuffe is common-sense incarnate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-crafted comedy gives intelligent female characters central roles and celebrates their wit and common sense; avoid sentimental depictions that deny such active intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance satire with humane sympathy; avoid mere cynicism
rubrics_metrics.description: We have the heavy moralizings by which we are outwearied... perversions of the idea of life... Comedy justly treated... throws no infamous reflection upon life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire should be applied with humane sympathy; cynical or moralizing poses wear out audiences and misrepresent life. Comedy should expose faults but not degrade humanity.
